subject: Urgent: 429 surge causing latency amplification for NimbleRetail
messages:
From: Asha Patel <support@nimble-retail.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: platform@nimble-retail.com
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observed surge in 429s and p99 regressions over last 8 hours

Hi Hannah,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 429s around 02:30 UTC this morning — our p95 latency has risen from ~220ms to ~2.8s and p99 is regularly hitting 6–9s. Concurrently, error rates (5xx + 429) climbed from 0.2% to ~3.7%. The spike correlates with heavy retry activity from our backend clients; downstream queues are filling and timeouts are cascading.

Impact: customer-facing search is timing out intermittently (users report long page loads). This is causing increased support tickets and a drop in conversion on top-of-funnel flows.

We dug into Datadog and captured spans and token bucket traces (link below). The traces show repeated client retries immediately after receiving 429s, which then pile up and increase tail latency for other requests.

Datadog: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/xyz/nimbleretail-api-overview
Attached: dd-logs-20260503.txt (sample spans)

Can you confirm whether any rate-limiter or per-tenant throttling changes were deployed overnight? We need an ETA for a mitigation and whether you can roll back.

Thanks — Asha

--
Asha Patel
Platform Engineer, NimbleRetail
support@nimble-retail.com

Next steps we propose:
- Immediate call (15m) to correlate logs and topology
- Temporary mitigation: relax per-tenant burst thresholds and re-enable randomized backoff jitter on retries
- If mitigation fails, rollback the limiter change

I can join a call now. Stephanie — please prep a brief exec summary for NimbleRetail and share any SLO/credit implications.

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observed surge in 429s and p99 regressions over last 8 hours

Quick summary from SRE triage: we rolled a rate-limiter config at 03:40 UTC that changed per-tenant token refill logic from "leaky bucket" to a batched refill intended to improve throughput. The batch refill unintentionally synchronized refill boundaries across tenants under bursty traffic patterns. That synchronization makes 429 responses burstier; combined with clients that retry aggressively (no jitter), this creates a feedback loop: 429 -> immediate retry -> concentrated burst -> more 429s -> queueing -> higher latency.

Evidence: repeated token-depleted spans in the dd-logs and a stair-step pattern of request rates matching the batch window. I've attached the config diff and extracted logs.

Temporary mitigations we can execute immediately (10–20m):
- Re-enable jittered exponential backoff on the gateway (server-side enforcement until client updates)
- Restore previous refill behavior for per-tenant buckets (rollback config)
- Add a short server-side randomized hold (50–200ms) for clients that hit 429 more than 3x in 30s to dampen retries

I'll open an incident (PD-8871) and run the rollback if approved. If rollback looks clean we can push it and monitor for 30–60 minutes.

Attachments: redwood-rate-limiter-config.diff, pd-incident-8871.txt

-David

--
David Kim
SRE, Redwood Inference

We can rollback the rate-limiter change to the prior commit and route traffic to a fallback model bundle to reduce per-request CPU while we stabilize. I have a safe rollback patch that preserves the new metrics instrumentation; I can deploy it in ~20 minutes and validate.

Action list I'm executing now:
1) Trigger rollback (10–20m)
2) Apply short server-side retry-damp (50–200ms randomized hold)
3) Temporarily increase per-tenant burst allowance for NimbleRetail (policy override)
4) Monitor p95/p99 and error-rate dashboards; report back in 15m increments

I'll post logs and the deployment link to PD-8871 and HubSpot (NR-4471) as soon as done.

-Marissa

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-04T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update and exec summary — NimbleRetail 429 amplification (PD-8871)

Executive summary for leadership:
- Impact: NimbleRetail reported a production incident starting 2026-05-03 02:30 UTC causing elevated p95/p99 latencies and a 3.7% error spike (429s + 5xx). Checkout timeouts observed by customer.
- Root cause: rate-limiter refill behavior change created synchronized token depletion under bursty traffic which, paired with aggressive client retries, produced a retry-amplification feedback loop.
- Mitigations applied: rollback of limiter change (Marissa) + server-side retry damping and per-tenant burst override. Initial metrics show p95 dropped from ~2.8s to ~250ms and p99 improving from ~7–9s to ~600–900ms within 30 minutes. Error rate down to ~0.4%.

Open asks / decisions required:
1) Approve a follow-up rollback-release postmortem timeline and customer-facing note (draft ready) — ETA 4 hours to finalize
2) Approve a temporary compensation/credit to NimbleRetail if SLA window extends beyond 48 hours (Stephanie to advise)
3) Authorize SRE overtime for two engineers for incident hardening (David/Marissa) — estimate 8–12 hours total

Attached artifacts: dd-logs-20260503.txt, redwood-rate-limiter-config.diff, pd-incident-8871.txt
Links: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/xyz/nimbleretail-api-overview, https://pagerduty.com/incidents/8871, https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/NR-4471

I'll schedule a 30-minute postmortem tomorrow; Marissa, David, please bring timeline and repro steps. Stephanie — please coordinate customer comms and commercial ask.

-Hannah
